anna: Bringing up ORION-70k (int4) for long-context evals — seeing divergence when prefix length crosses ~32768 tokens. Root test set: longprefill-1k (mixed docs). Sharing quick notes and repro commands.

miguel: Can you paste the exact command + a tiny log snippet? :eyes:

anna: Yep — minimal repro I used locally: 
```
run_local_eval --model orion-70k --quant int4 --ctx 65536 --prefill_file longprefill-1k.json --seed 42 --batch 1
```
Log tail after generating token ~32780: 
```
[2026-03-22T14:12:03Z] kv_cache: write index=32770 len=16 window=65536
[2026-03-22T14:12:03Z] kv_cache: write index=32788 len=32 window=65536
[2026-03-22T14:12:03Z] kv_cache: index_rollover detected -> pointer wrapped to 0
[2026-03-22T14:12:03Z] generation: context_mismatch at token 32789
```

cheng: Hmm, interesting. We've seen pointer wrap when prefill chunks align badly with our internal tiling. Could be RoPE index truncation on quant path (int4) vs fp16. Did you compare identical run in fp16?

anna: Yes — fp16 run with same seed and prefix didn't show the pointer wrap or the context_mismatch. Perplexity delta on longprefill set: int4 +1.3 vs fp16; but the visible failure mode is divergence after wrap.

miguel: Do you see any checksum or fingerprint mismatch from the prefill verifier? `prefill-checker` outputs?

anna: Ran it. Short output pasted: 
```
prefill-checker --verify longprefill-1k.json --model orion-70k --quant int4
> chunk_0 ok
> chunk_1 ok
> chunk_2 partial_mismatch @offset 32768
> aborting: detected kv-index overflow pattern
```

cheng: That offset is suspicious — 32768 is exactly 2^15, and our RoPE rotate arithmetic has a signed/unsigned interaction in the int4 pointer math path. Possibly a cast from int32->int16 in an int4 packing routine causing wrap at 32768.

anna: I dug into server logs; the int4 kernel emits an index bundle with `idx16 = idx & 0xffff` at serialization. Looks like we didn't bump the packing width when switching to 64k contexts.

miguel: Okay — two orthogonal experiments to run: (A) force `ropereset=legacy` vs `ropereset=scaled` to see RoPE handling impact; (B) run quantization micropatch that avoids `idx16` packing (fall back to 32-bit index) to confirm if bug is packing-related.

anna: Ran experiment A quickly. With `--rope-mode scaled` divergence still present but onset delayed (around 41200 tokens). With `--rope-mode legacy` it reproduces at ~32768 again. So scaling changes where the mismatch surfaces but doesn't fix packing.

miguel: That aligns with a pure pointer-wrap theory. What's the hit for switching the packing to 32-bit? Memory + perf?

cheng: Rough estimate: per-kv-entry increases by 4 bytes -> ~3.5% RAM increase for 65k contexts. Perf impact negligible in CUDA kernel, main cost in network serialization. Worth a canary.

anna: I prepared a quick canary plan:
- canary A: int4 + packing-fix (no idx16) + rope-mode scaled + chunked-prefill=8k
- canary B: int4 + packing-fix + rope-mode legacy + kv-safety-limit=60000
Regression criteria: hallucination rate on longprefill set increases by >2x or perplexity delta >2.0 -> rollback.

miguel: +1 to both. Also add a synthetic test that abuses prefix lengths across the boundary: create prefixes at [32760..32780] to make reproduction deterministic.

anna: I'll enqueue 500 eval examples over longprefill-1k and synthetic boundary set. ETA 2h. Pushing canary now.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deployment started: orion-70k-int4-canary-a & orion-70k-int4-canary-b (ids: canary-101, canary-102). Logs stream will be available at /deploys/canary-101.

ci-bot: ci-bot: prefill-checker job queued (job id 8783). Will post pass/fail once finished.

anna: Quick heads-up — if canary shows no regressions we'll land packing fix in next minor release and roll to dedicated. If it reproduces in canary, we'll revert and open a hotfix branch.

cheng: If packing fix goes in, follow-up: add unit test for large-context pointer arithmetic (prefix sizes up to 65536) and a fuzz harness to vary chunk alignments.

miguel: Thanks. Keep us posted. If you need help triaging logs or adding traces for `kv.index` events, ping me. :thumbsup:

anna: Will do — posting initial canary perf summary once CI finishes.

anna: tl;dr: likely int4 serialization packing bug causing Kv-index wrap at 32768 -> triggers generation divergence for long prefill. Canary + tests in flight.
